q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT TMP.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(TMP.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM (SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, P.EMPLOYEE_ID, E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS FROM EMPLOYEE E INNER JOIN PROJECT P ON E.EMPLOYEE_ID = P.EMPLOYEE_ID ) AS TMP GROUP BY TMP.PROJECT_ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT TMP.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(TMP.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM (SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, P.EMPLOYEE_ID, E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS FROM EMPLOYEE E INNER JOIN PROJECT P ON E.EMPLOYEE_ID = P.EMPLOYEE_ID ) AS TMP GROUP BY TMP.PROJECT_ID
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. Both queries compute the average experience years of employees per project by joining the EMPLOYEE and PROJECT tables and then grouping by PROJECT_ID. Q2 uses a subquery (TMP) to first join the tables and then computes the average, which is logically the same as Q1.
